summary: Runbook Console access intermittently denied after Okta group assignment; provisioning window misaligned
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers report receiving 403 when opening the internal Runbook Console immediately after their Okta access request is approved. The approval shows in Okta but the Runbook Console denies access for a short window (2–6 minutes) before access becomes available without further action.

Impact: Affects ~8 engineers across multiple teams during onboarding and emergency on-call escalations when immediate runbook access is required. No broader production customer impact, but blocks triage and incident responses during the window.

Observed behavior: After Support approves a request in the internal portal (Okta group assignment via SCIM/webhook), users either see a 403 on the Runbook Console or an "insufficient privileges" banner. Refreshing the page after ~3–5 minutes usually resolves it. The Runbook Console logs show a policy evaluation failure citing missing group membership for the user at the time of the request.

Environment: prod us-west; identity-syncs handled by okta-sync service; runbook UI behind identity-proxy (cookie-based SSO).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a test user in Okta and request Runbook Console access via the internal support flow.
2) Approve the request in the support portal (triggers Okta group assignment).
3) Immediately sign in to runbook.redwood-internal and observe 403; retry after a few minutes to observe successful access.

Logs & traces:
- runbook-ui request-id=7f2a3c logs: "policy_evaluation: failed - missing_group:rbac-runbook-editor" at 2026-03-10T14:22:11Z
- okta-sync trace shows SCIM patch succeeded at 2026-03-10T14:22:07Z; webhook delivered to identity-proxy at 14:22:07Z.
- identity-proxy cache hit/miss pattern: cache TTL eviction observed; user group lookup returned stale cache for 3 consecutive requests.

Initial hypothesis: The runbook UI uses a read-through RBAC cache in identity-proxy with a TTL of 3 minutes. Okta group assignment arrives, but the identity-proxy is serving cached user role mappings until the TTL expires. In some cases the SCIM webhook and group-sync tasks race with cache refresh, causing a 2–6 minute window where the principal appears unassigned. A secondary hypothesis is that a background job that patches internal role-mappings (backfill) has been deferred/queued, increasing the gap.

Immediate workaround: Advise support to instruct users to wait ~5 minutes after approval before accessing the console or to manually trigger a "Force refresh" on the identity-proxy health endpoint (internal-only). Documented a temporary runbook for on-call.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short-term (low risk): Reduce identity-proxy RBAC cache TTL from 180s to 30s for runbook-principal lookups; monitor error rate. (Config PR prepared: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412)
- Medium-term: Add a webhook-triggered cache invalidation path: when Okta SCIM patch succeeds, post an invalidation to identity-proxy for the affected user.
- Long-term: Evaluate replacing read-through cache with subscription-based user state updates to eliminate TTL windows.

Owner: Miguel Ortega (identity infra).
